subject: Commercial terms: multi-year prepay — invoicing entity & VAT/withholding clarifications
messages:
From: Lukas Meier <lukas.meier@stromline.de>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Cc: Anja Vogel <anja.vogel@stromline.de>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 14:15:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial — initial terms (multi-year prepay)

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the proposal — we had a quick procurement review and a couple of high-level questions before we move to legal:

- We prefer a 3-year prepaid commit (annual invoices) with a 20% term discount in year-1, stepping to 15% in year-2 and 10% in year-3. Is that something Redwood can accommodate?
- Our finance team is in Germany; we need a German invoicing entity to reclaim VAT. Can Redwood invoice from an EU entity? Alternatively, what documentation do you need so we can process VAT correctly?
- Also: we sometimes have up to 5% withholding tax on certain service suppliers unless the supplier has an EU-based taxable presence. Any guidance on withholding treatment for your invoices?

If helpful, I can loop in our tax advisor. We’d like to confirm high-level commercials by next week.

Best,
Lukas
Procurement — Stromline GmbH

[Attachment: Stromline_preferred_payment_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Lukas Meier <lukas.meier@stromline.de>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 16:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial — initial terms (multi-year prepay)

Hi Lukas — thanks for the clarity and the preferred payment profile. Quick responses inline: 

- Term discount: we can do a 3-year prepay with an escalating discount schedule, but our standard multi-year prepay savings are structured slightly differently to align with revenue recognition and refund windows. We can match your list (20/15/10) on a commercial basis — I’ll flag to finance for invoicing timing and accounting treatment.

- Invoicing entity / VAT: Redwood can invoice either from our US entity or our EU branch (Redwood Inference EU B.V.). We typically prefer EU invoicing for customers who need to reclaim VAT. I’ll confirm the exact legal name and VAT ID.

- Withholding tax: if Redwood invoices from the EU entity and the services are supplied from within the EU, withholding is usually not applicable. If we invoice from the US entity, there’s a risk of local withholding depending on German rules. Evelyn, can you advise on the withholding exposure and whether we should route invoices through EU entity?

I’ll attach an updated term sheet reflecting a 3-year prepay with the 20/15/10 schedule for your review.

Next step: can we confirm which invoicing entity Stromline prefers and whether you’ll require any tax forms (W-8/W-9 equivalent or Certificate of Tax Residency)?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: 20251103_Redwood_Stromline_MultiYear_TermSheet.pdf (pdf)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:25:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial — initial terms (multi-year prepay)

Camila / Aditya — quick finance note for routing: 

- Redwood Inference EU B.V. (our NL entity) can issue invoices with a valid EU VAT ID. That will simplify VAT recovery for Stromline.
- Withholding: services provided by Redwood EU are not generally subject to German withholding tax. If we invoice from our US entity, Stromline may request a reduced withholding or documentation — we don’t have a local German fiscal presence in that case.
- Ramp schedule: to support revenue recognition and to make customer success handoffs simple, we prefer annual invoicing on the anniversary date with the prepay applied at contract start. Given Stromline’s usage growth plan, we can structure a staged delivery schedule (yearly buckets) with volume-based credits if actual usage is below the prepay bucket.

Markus, if Stromline requests invoicing split across EU and US entity for tax reasons, we need approval for mixed invoicing.

Evelyn
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial — multi-year prepay (tax note)

Camila — a couple of EU-side clarifications for the thread to share with Stromline: 

1) Legal invoicing name: Redwood Inference EU B.V. — VAT ID: NL813456789B01.
2) We can accommodate your 3-year prepay as a single upfront payment with annual internal allocation, or as three annual prepay invoices at the customer’s preference; both are acceptable commercially but differ for us accounting-wise.

If Stromline prefers annual prepayments in EUR, we should agree on an FX clause: either (a) lock the EUR amount at signing (Redwood bears FX after that), or (b) invoice in EUR based on the invoice date FX rate. We recommend option (a) for predictability; if Stromline prefers (b), we can accept but will include a +/- 2% margin to offset FX volatility.

3) Withholding: if invoiced from Redwood EU B.V., there should be no German withholding. If they ask for US invoices, they may apply WHT — we would need a treaty certificate or other documentation to reduce it.

Happy to jump on a short call with Stromline tax if they want to close this.

— Markus
Director, International Finance (Redwood EU)

From: Anja Vogel <anja.vogel@stromline.de>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lukas Meier <lukas.meier@stromline.de>, procurement@stromline.de
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2025 09:42:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Commercial terms: multi-year prepay — invoicing entity & VAT/withholding clarifications

Hi Camila / Markus — thanks for the detail and the VAT ID. A few follow-ups from our tax team (attached):

- Stromline would prefer Redwood to invoice from Redwood Inference EU B.V. and on an annual prepay cadence (one invoice per year).
- We’d like the EUR amounts fixed at signing to avoid budgeting headaches. Can Redwood accept locked EUR pricing for the 3-year term?
- For the FX clause: if you insist on invoice-date FX, we will need the +/- margin removed; otherwise we prefer fixed EUR amounts.
- On withholding: we will not apply withholding if the invoice is from your EU entity and the VAT ID is present.

If you can confirm the fixed-EUR approach and send an updated term sheet reflecting annual invoices and the 20/15/10 discount, we can route to legal and aim to sign within 5 business days.

Best regards,
Anja Vogel
Head of Finance — Stromline GmbH

[Attachment: 20251117_Stromline_Tax_Info.pdf (pdf)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Anja Vogel <anja.vogel@stromline.de>, Lukas Meier <lukas.meier@stromline.de>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 14:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Final commercial confirmation & next steps (DocuSign link enclosed)

Anja / Lukas — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming Redwood positions: 

- Invoicing entity: Redwood Inference EU B.V. (VAT ID NL813456789B01) — we will issue one EUR invoice per year.
- Pricing: we will lock EUR amounts at signing for the full 3-year term (no invoice-date FX).
- Discounts: 20% off list in year-1, 15% year-2, 10% year-3 — applied to the annual prepay invoice.
- Ramp schedule / usage credits: we will allocate the prepaid units per year on invoice anniversary with a standard true‑up mechanism (credits for unused units within the contract year, expiry rules in the term sheet).
- Withholding: not applicable for invoices issued by Redwood Inference EU B.V. per our counsel.

I have uploaded an updated term sheet and prepared a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/SL-8721. Please review and sign; once countersigned we will issue the year-1 invoice and schedule onboarding with Customer Success.

If you prefer a short call to walk tax/legal through the mechanics, happy to coordinate — propose Wed 19 Nov at 10:00 CET.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
